risks.risk: Exact model/brand mismatch (pricing depends heavily on the specific industrial model and capabilities).
risks.proof: A close-up photo of the machine’s nameplate/serial/model label (usually on the head or side of the body) with the text clearly readable.
risks.if_unproven: Price as an unverified industrial sewing machine with unknown model/capability (worst-case for value).

risks.risk: Working condition not confirmed (industrial machines can have hidden mechanical/electrical faults).
risks.proof: A short video of the machine sewing at speed (show needle moving, feed working, and consistent stitch formation) plus a close-up of the stitch/needle area while running.
risks.if_unproven: Price as not proven/assume may need service (worst-case for value).

risks.risk: Missing/incorrect accessories (presser feet, bobbins, needles, thread guides, manuals) affect usability and cost to complete.
risks.proof: A photo inventory laid out: all included presser feet, bobbins, needles, tools, and any manuals/warranty papers.

risks.risk: Power compatibility and electrical condition (voltage, plug type, and motor health).
risks.proof: A photo of the power rating label (voltage/Hz) and a video showing it powering on and running smoothly.
risks.if_unproven: Price assuming potential electrical servicing may be needed (worst-case).

risks.risk: Transport damage or misalignment (common with heavy industrial machines).
risks.proof: Photos of the machine head alignment and a video showing smooth operation without unusual noise/vibration.

proof_requests: Close-up, readable photo of the brand/model nameplate (confirm “EMel” and “EM 8500”).
Video of the machine sewing continuously (needle + feed + stitch result visible).
Photo inventory of included accessories (presser feet, bobbins, needles, tools, manuals).
Photo of electrical/power rating label and confirmation of voltage compatibility for Abuja.
response.reason: The photos show an industrial sewing machine setup, but the brand/model (“EMel EM 8500”) is not readable/confirmable from the images, and working condition is not proven. Without the exact model and a run test, a reliable worst-case price can’t be set confidently.
